text:
morgan: incident-bot just paged us for rising paged-attention fragmentation in us-west-2; multiple containers restarting with OOMs and a handful of node flaps. observed gradual RSS growth starting ~22:40 UTC.

incident-bot: [ALERT] paged_attention_fragmentation=0.81 on pool-usw2-gpu-11 \u2022 triggered at 2025-10-17T22:41:12Z

developer-bot: svc/stream-infer-9 restart spike detected (OOM_EXIT)

devon: I'm on call. pulling pmap/heapdump from affected host 10.12.2.33 now

sasha: were there any long seq jobs or stress tests on those nodes?

morgan: there were some long-context evals (seq 14k) queued overnight but fragmentation trend begins an hour earlier.

anil: host snapshot (10.12.2.33) - nvidia-smi shows near full memory on GPU0:

```
GPU0 MemUsed 24460 MiB / 24576 MiB
PID 6120 python - rss 24.2G (kv-holder)
PID 6199 python - rss 900M (worker)
```

tia: kernel logs show repeated driver Xid 31 messages prior to restarts - looks like user-space page faults followed by driver resets.

devon: initial reads indicate slab fragmentation - many tiny live allocations held across KV pages preventing coalescing, and compaction is failing under contention. could be allocator change in last runtime deploy.

morgan: confirmed - runtime patch 2025-10-17T21:10 rolled last night to tweak tiny-alloc fast-path.

sasha: immediate remediation plan? can we run compaction safely or do a restart?

devon: safe approach: 1) divert new traffic off 10.12.2.33 2) send graceful quiesce to KV owner (SIGUSR1 implemented for pause) 3) call /admin/kv/compact 4) restart process if compaction clears fragmentation.

morgan: switching routing to prefer-smaller-kv variants for the pool to reduce pressure (expect ~10% latency bump).

anil: SIGUSR1 sent to pid 6120; KV refcount dropping from ~130k -> ~8k in ~30s.

anil: invoking compaction: `curl -X POST -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN\" https://10.12.2.33:8443/admin/kv/compact?timeout=180s`

anil: compaction logs:

[INFO] kv_compact: merged 9 pages, reclaimed 1.7GB
[WARN] kv_compact: slab 0x7f9... lock contention, retry=1
[ERROR] kv_compact: slab 0x7f9... coalesce failed: EBUSY

tia: EBUSY during compaction correlates with driver Xid noise. compaction is contending with active kernels that still hold transient pointers. we need a full process quiesce to avoid repeated failures.

devon: will send a stronger pause and retry compaction. sequence: SIGUSR1, wait 45s, re-run compact. if EBUSY persists, fall back to process restart to unblock.

sasha: customer impact? support tickets?

morgan: roughly 14% of requests in the region got transient 503s/timeouts during routing switchover. Support ticket INC-2025-9133 created and linked to alerts. no SLA breach yet.

support-bot: New ticket INC-2025-9133 - "timeouts and retries on generate endpoint" attached to alerts.

anil: second compaction attempt after extended quiesce succeeded; freed contiguous pages ~2.4GB. fragmentation dropped from 0.79 -> 0.33.

devon: restarting kv-owner pid 6120 to ensure driver state clean and to pick up allocator toggles. planning rolling restarts across pool after compaction to avoid recurrence.

morgan: restart done; monitoring shows no further OOMs on 10.12.2.33. fragmentation trending down across pool.

tia: still logging occasional Xid 31s but not followed by OOMs now. likely residual but reduced.

sasha: root cause summary?

devon: probable regression: tiny-alloc fast-path optimization increased churn of small allocations, raising internal fragmentation of the KV paged allocator. compaction raced with active kernels (lock contention -> EBUSY), which prevented timely coalescing and led to gradual memory creep then OOMs.

action items:
- revert tiny-alloc fast-path patch until compaction-safe path is implemented (owner: devon)
- add a kvcache_fragmentation_warn threshold at 0.5 with automated gentle-compact during low-load windows (owner: sasha)
- emit slab lock contention and compaction EBUSY as metrics/alerts (owner: anil)
- add a quiesce endpoint test and integration test for compaction correctness (owner: devon)
- postmortem + customer comms (owner: morgan)

morgan: scheduling revert canary at 03:15 UTC. handing off to next on-call at 02:00 UTC - please escalate if compaction errors or Xid 31 -> OOM reappear.

sasha: thanks everyone. I'll draft the postmortem and coordinate with support for customer updates. closing thread and tracking follow-ups in INC-2025-9133. :thumbsup:
